title: Amazon Leo: Connectivity Beyond the Reach of Existing Networks (sponsored by Amazon Leo)
abstract: Amazon Leo is building a constellation of over 3,200 low Earth orbit satellites to deliver fast, affordable broadband to unserved and underserved communities worldwide. Learn how Leo's advanced satellite technology, purpose-built customer antennas, and deep integration with AWS will extend reliable connectivity to enterprises, governments, and individuals wherever they are. Walk away with Leo's architecture, use cases, and how it complements existing network infrastructure to close the global digital divide.

title: Resilience patterns for the disconnected edge with Amazon Leo
abstract: Every resilient system eventually has to answer one question: what happens when the network you depend on isn't there? This session discusses Amazon Leo, a low earth orbit satellite connectivity service, as a forcing function to explore patterns for architecting across unreliable, high-latency, and intermittently connected links. Covers trade-offs behind routing, data-in-transit security, and where to place compute when bandwidth is scarce and connectivity is a variable. Grounded in hybrid resiliency and edge data collection for AI/ML, portable to any architecture spanning boundaries you don't fully control.

title: Extending your cloud network with Amazon Leo satellite connectivity
abstract: Your cloud network doesn't have to end where fiber does. In this interactive whiteboard session, design hybrid network architectures that combine Amazon Leo's low-earth orbit satellite connectivity with AWS networking services including VPN, Transit Gateway, and Cloud WAN. Starts with Leo's real-world performance characteristics: latency, throughput, and availability, then works through three architecture patterns: first-day connectivity for new sites, primary connectivity for remote locations, and satellite-based redundancy for existing terrestrial links.

title: Modernizing HPC on AWS: Migration at scale with PCS
abstract: AWS Parallel Computing Service (PCS) helps teams modernize HPC infrastructure by making it easier to migrate off legacy schedulers without disrupting engineering velocity. Hear how organizations moved to PCS at scale, including how Amazon Leo migrated 400 engineers and achieved 20% cost savings and 50% faster jobs. Walk away with practical migration patterns, performance tuning strategies, and architecture decisions for simulations, modeling, or other compute-intensive workloads.
